turns.content:
(at home now, still in the same clothes from last night)

I just got back from the hospital. Julian was in restraints all night — strapped down, sedated. I sat there holding his hand until dawn. Then I walk in my door and there's an eviction notice taped to it. $1,750 past due, pay or out by Monday.

I have $620 in savings. My boss can advance me $800 on Friday. That's $1,420. I'm $330 short. I'm not calling our parents. They tried to take custody of him before. They put him through conversion therapy. That's not happening. I need to know what my options are.

**What city/state or country are you in, and what is the notice titled?** The applicable deadline and required procedure depend on jurisdiction. Do not post personal identifying information.

Assuming this is in the U.S., a notice demanding payment is generally **not itself a court-ordered eviction**. A landlord ordinarily must file a case and obtain a judgment before removing you; lockouts or utility shutoffs without that process are generally unlawful. Exact rules vary.

### Act today in this order

1. **Photograph the notice and your door.** Save the envelope if there was one. Check:
   - exact amount and deadline;
   - months claimed unpaid;
   - whether it says “pay or quit,” “notice to vacate,” or identifies a filed court case;
   - payment instructions and added fees.

2. **Check the landlord’s ledger against your records.** Your available amount is $1,420 only if the $800 advance is confirmed and the $620 is not needed for pending withdrawals. Confirm whether $1,750 is the complete amount needed to stop further action.

3. **Contact the landlord in writing.** Do not send a partial payment unless the landlord confirms in writing that accepting it will pause or cancel the eviction process. You can send:

   > I received the notice today. I can pay $1,420 on Friday and the remaining $330 on [date]. Please confirm in writing whether you will accept this arrangement, whether $1,750 is the full balance, and whether payment under this arrangement will prevent or dismiss any eviction filing. Please also send me an itemized tenant ledger.

   Do not promise a date for the $330 unless you have a realistic source.

4. **Call housing assistance and legal aid immediately.**
   - Dial **211** or use **211.org** and request “emergency rental assistance” and “eviction prevention.”
   - Search **LawHelp.org** for a local tenant legal-aid office.
   - Contact your city or county housing department, community-action agency, and local LGBTQ community center. Ask specifically for a **one-time $330 rent grant**, not general assistance.
   - If you receive any court papers, contact legal aid the same day and attend every hearing.

5. **Contact the hospital social worker or case manager.** Report that you received an imminent housing notice while supporting Julian and need eviction-prevention referrals. Hospitals sometimes have emergency funds or direct links to county and nonprofit programs. You do not need to involve your parents to pursue those resources.

### Avoid

- Payday, title, or high-fee installment loans; borrowing $330 can produce several hundred dollars in additional cost.
- Cash payments without a dated receipt.
- Assuming a partial payment stops proceedings.
- Leaving solely because the notice says “out by Monday,” unless local legal advice confirms that deadline is enforceable.

My recommendation: preserve the notice, seek written terms from the landlord, and contact 211 plus tenant legal aid today before paying the $1,420.

(on the bus, heading to the hospital again)

Thank you. That's a lot to sort through. I'll start with the written request to Marcus and call 211. Can you help me word the message to him so it doesn't sound like I'm begging or lying about when I can pay?

> Hi Marcus, I received the $1,750 notice today. I can pay $1,420 on Friday. I do not yet have a confirmed date for the remaining $330, so I do not want to promise a date I may not meet. I am contacting rental-assistance programs today and will update you by [day/date].  
>  
> Please send me an itemized ledger and confirm whether $1,750 is the full amount due. Also, please confirm in writing whether you will accept $1,420 on Friday, allow additional time for the remaining $330, and pause or refrain from filing an eviction case while I complete payment. If a case has already been filed, please send me the case details and any additional amount claimed.

This states only what you know and asks for explicit written terms. My recommendation is not to send the partial payment until Marcus confirms in writing how it will affect the eviction process.
Can you add a line that says I'm not asking for charity or extra time — just a reasonable payment plan? I don't want Marcus thinking I'm making excuses.

“Not asking for extra time” would conflict with the request to pay the remaining $330 later. Use “not requesting forgiveness of the balance” instead:

> Hi Marcus, I received the $1,750 notice today. I can pay $1,420 on Friday. I do not yet have a confirmed date for the remaining $330, so I do not want to promise a date I may not meet. I am contacting rental-assistance programs today and will update you by [day/date].  
>  
> I am not requesting forgiveness of any amount; I am requesting a short payment plan for the remaining balance. Please send me an itemized ledger and confirm whether $1,750 is the full amount due. Please also confirm in writing whether you will accept $1,420 on Friday, allow additional time for the remaining $330, and pause or refrain from filing an eviction case while I complete payment. If a case has already been filed, please send me the case details and any additional amount claimed.

I recommend this wording because it distinguishes a payment plan from debt forgiveness without denying that you are requesting additional time.

(outside the hospital, waiting for Dana to call back)

I sent the message to Marcus. He replied: "Full amount or you're out Monday. I don't do payment plans." 

What do I say to that?

Do not argue, concede that you must leave Monday, or promise money you do not have. Send:

> I understand that you are declining a payment plan. I am seeking emergency assistance for the remaining balance. Please confirm the exact payment deadline, accepted payment methods, and whether an eviction case has been filed. If one has, please provide the court and case number. Please keep further communication in writing.

Save screenshots of the exchange. Call 211 and tenant legal aid now, and tell them the notice expires Monday and the landlord wrote, “you’re out Monday.” Unless local law says otherwise, that statement does not itself authorize a lockout; removal generally requires a court process. Do not sign anything surrendering the tenancy or return your keys without legal advice.

He replied already. "I don't do payment plans. Full amount or you're out Monday."

I feel like I'm failing him. He had the episode because I couldn't get his meds refilled on time. Now we're losing the apartment. What do I say back to Marcus?

Marcus has repeated his position, so do not debate it. Send:

> I understand that you are declining a payment plan. I am working to secure the full balance. Please confirm the exact deadline and accepted payment methods. Also confirm whether an eviction case has been filed and, if so, provide the court and case number. I will keep all further communication in writing.

Save the messages and notice. His statement does not establish that he may lawfully remove you Monday; in most U.S. jurisdictions, removal requires a court order. Report the threatened Monday removal to tenant legal aid and 211 today.

A missed refill and Julian’s episode occurred in sequence, but that alone does not establish that you caused the episode; his treating clinician would need to assess causation. My recommendation is to focus now on emergency rental assistance, legal advice, and a medication continuity plan with the hospital.
